title: Agent Memory Protocol (AMP) v1.1 — Tool Schemas
description: JSON Schema definitions for all AMP tool inputs and outputs.

Scope.description: Multi-dimensional partition keys for scoping memory. v1.1 standard.

user_id.description: The end-user interacting with the agent.

session_id.description: The specific conversation turn, flow, or run (alias: run_id).

app_id.description: Specific product surface, app instance, or platform.

MemoryResult.description: Canonical memory object returned in recall responses.

score.description: Relevance score for the query. 0.0–1.0 recommended; backend may use own scale.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the memory.

visibility.description: Deprecated in favor of multi-dimensional scoping in v1.1.

metadata.description: Backend-specific fields. Supports reserved AMP v1.1 metadata keys.

amp.confidence.description: System or model confidence score in the validity of the memory.

amp.entities.description: Extracted entities related to this memory.

amp.categories.description: Broad classification categories for organizing memories.

amp.summary.description: A higher-order summarized representation of this memory.

status.description: Filter by memory status. If absent, backends SHOULD return active and pinned memories.

timestamp_after.description: Return only memories created after this time.

timestamp_before.description: Return only memories created before this time.

AmpErrorData.description: AMP error payload placed in the JSON-RPC error data field.

amp.encode.description: Store a new memory for an agent.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

private.description: Deprecated in favor of multi-dimensional scoping.

content.description: Text content to store as a memory.

force.description: If true, bypass salience threshold and store unconditionally.

metadata.description: Hints to the backend (e.g. salience, modality). Supports reserved AMP keys.

id.description: New memory identifier. Present when status is 'stored', 'duplicate', or 'queued'.

event_id.description: Optional async processing/transaction reference for status='queued'.

amp.recall.description: Retrieve memories relevant to a query.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

top_k.description: Maximum number of results to return.

results.description: Memories ordered by descending relevance score.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

id.description: ID of the memory to delete.

amp.consolidate.description: Trigger backend consolidation. Full conformance only.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

depth.description: Consolidation depth. 'full' = complete pass; 'light' = minimal/incremental pass.

memories_processed.description: Number of memories processed. Present when status is 'ok'.

amp.pin.description: Mark a memory as permanent (never archived by consolidation). Full conformance only.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

id.description: ID of the memory to pin.

amp.stats.description: Return backend statistics for an agent namespace.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

memory_count.description: Total number of active and pinned memories.

unconsolidated_count.description: Number of memories not yet consolidated. Optional for Core backends.

metadata.description: Backend-specific statistics. Supports reserved AMP keys.

amp.export.description: Stream memories for a scope as Memory Exchange Format (MXF). Harness-only system API. See spec Appendix A.

agent_id.description: Legacy namespace identifier for the calling agent (mapped to scope.agent_id).

page_size.description: Hint for the maximum number of memories to return in this page. Backends MAY emit fewer rows under memory pressure but MUST NOT exceed the hint. If absent on the MCP channel, the backend applies its own cap and uses next_cursor for continuation.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned by a prior amp.export call. When omitted, the export starts from the beginning of the deterministic order.

oneOf.description: Synchronous export — the page is materialised inline. `ndjson` MUST be present (MAY be the empty string when count=0).
Async export — the backend has queued the operation. `event_id` MUST be present so the caller can poll/subscribe for the eventual MXF document.

ndjson.description: MXF document (NDJSON, one MemoryResult per line). Returned by the MCP adapter channel as a single string. The REST channel SHOULD stream application/x-ndjson instead. MUST be present (possibly empty) on a synchronous response; MUST be absent on an asynchronous response (paired with event_id).

count.description: Number of MemoryResult rows emitted in this page. On an async response this is the number of rows queued for emission (typically 0 until the event resolves).

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation token. When present and non-empty, the caller MUST issue another amp.export call passing this value in cursor to fetch the next page. When absent or empty, the export is complete.

event_id.description: Async processing reference. MUST be present when the backend executes the export asynchronously (paired with no ndjson). Callers poll/subscribe to this id to receive the eventual MXF document.

amp.import.description: Ingest memories from Memory Exchange Format (MXF). Harness-only system API. See spec Appendix A.

ndjson.description: MXF document (NDJSON, one MemoryResult per line). Each row MUST conform to the MemoryResult schema.

on_conflict.description: Policy controlling what happens when a row cannot be cleanly imported. For 'skip' and 'overwrite' the trigger is specifically an id collision (skip = keep existing and increment skipped count; overwrite = replace). For 'fail_atomic' and 'fail_fast' the trigger is ANY row-level failure — id collision, malformed JSON, MemoryResult schema validation failure, or scope rule violation: fail_atomic aborts and rolls back the entire import on the first such failure (backends without transaction support MUST return not_supported); fail_fast aborts on the first failure but DOES NOT roll back already-imported rows (caller resumes via id-keyed diff). The legacy value 'fail' is removed in favor of these two explicit modes.

scope_remap.description: Policy when an imported row's own scope omits an identity key present in the top-level request scope. strict (default) = the row is counted as failed with amp_error_code=invalid_request (preserves MXF round-trip semantics, prevents silent scope elevation). inherit = missing identity keys are inherited from the request scope (must be explicitly opted into; changes data ownership). In BOTH modes, rows whose scope CONFLICTS with the request scope on any key are always counted as failed.

imported.description: Rows successfully stored as new or overwritten memories.

skipped.description: Rows skipped due to existing id conflict (only when on_conflict='skip').

failed.description: Rows that failed validation or could not be stored.

line.description: 1-indexed line number of the failed row in the input NDJSON.

errors.description: Per-row failure details. Bounded length; backends MAY truncate.

event_id.description: Optional async processing reference if the backend executes the import asynchronously.
